findings.title: parse_date silently drops DD/MM/YYYY input
findings.failure: Parse, Don't Validate. parse_date is supposed to accept the common date formats users actually submit and make failure explicit to the caller. It only handles YYYY-MM-DD and returns None for DD/MM/YYYY, and the caller at line 78 treats None as 'expired' and logs the user out. Conflating 'unparseable' with 'expired' in a single None turns bad input into a silent logout with no path for the user to recover.
findings.fix: Return Result<Date, ParseDateError> with a typed error on unrecognized input so the caller routes to the retry dialog instead of logging the user out; accept both formats explicitly.

findings.title: Phase 2 network-failure fallback is missing
findings.failure: Untested Path. Phase 2 is supposed to enumerate the failure modes of the API fetch so the fallback is buildable and testable. The phase's task list covers only the success path — no fallback UI, no retry logic specified. When the request fails users see a crash with no recovery path, and the plan can't be meaningfully tested under realistic conditions because the failure modes aren't enumerated.
findings.fix: Add a task under Phase 2 that specifies the fallback UI plus exponential-backoff retry, and a test scenario covering the network-failure path.

findings.title: AuthService mixes display and orchestration concerns
findings.failure: God Class. AuthService should expose only orchestration concerns — login, refresh, logout. It also formats and prints the login prompts and error screens inline, pulling terminal rendering into the auth module. Every UI tweak forces re-testing auth logic, headless contexts can't use the service, and consumers depending on auth get pulled into rendering code they don't need.
findings.fix: Split into src/auth/orchestration.rs (pure auth logic) and src/ui/auth_views.rs (rendering). Keep the auth interface narrow to the operations consumers actually need.
